name: Dhow Boat Decoration
summary: Traditional decorative elements found on dhows, the characteristic sailing vessels of the Arabian Peninsula.
description: Dhow decoration features geometric patterns, calligraphy, and floral motifs carved or painted onto the bow, stern, and transom of vessels, with regional variations reflecting different boat-building traditions. These decorative elements served both practical purposes (identifying ownership) and cultural significance, with many designs incorporating religious symbols and protective motifs for safe voyages.
culturalContext: Dhow decoration — the Indian Ocean sailing vessel's ornamental culture (Oman, Zanzibar, Gujarat, Kuwait) — carved prows (qarqab), painted eyes (nakhoda "compass eyes"), stitched-seam patterns, raked mast garlands and cargo-hold geometricains into working ships: the sea as canvas. Dhows carried the Swahili, Arabian and Indian coasts' trade for two millennia; surviving yards (Sur, Oman) and regattas (Al Gaffal) keep the craft, while museum dhows preserve the eye-and-carving grammar.
